about_blocks.text: Into Action Recovery 113B is a live-in recovery house for men at 13272 113B Avenue in the Whalley area of north Surrey. It is the third of Into Action Recovery Society's Surrey homes, alongside Bear Creek in Newton and the house on 100 Avenue, and it runs the same First Stage program.
about_blocks.html: Into Action Recovery 113B is a live-in recovery house for men at 13272 113B Avenue in the Whalley area of north Surrey. It is the third of Into Action Recovery Society's Surrey homes, alongside Bear Creek in Newton and the house on 100 Avenue, and it runs the same First Stage program.

about_blocks.text: The house is an ordinary suburban home with warm, lamp-lit rooms. Into Action's photos show a living room with dark leather sofas and a big TV, a small dining nook with a round table by the window, and bedrooms with a nightstand and a reading lamp by each bed. It feels like somebody's family house, and that is the idea; Into Action prefers home-like settings to clinical ones.

about_blocks.text: Into Action's program is built with repeat relapse in mind, and recovery.com lists repeated relapse alongside alcohol, opioids, fentanyl, cocaine and prescription drugs. The program answers that with time and repetition. Stays start at 60 days, with longer stays when the team thinks they will help. Every day includes education groups, process groups and one-to-one counselling, and step work is guided by staff who include a step coach. Relapse prevention planning runs through the whole stay.

about_blocks.text: Into Action is open about what it is not. It is not a medical or mental health facility, there is no nurse or doctor in the house, and detox has to be done before admission. Residents keep their own doctor or use the virtual clinic Into Action works with for prescriptions. If a man already has a counsellor or psychiatrist, the house supports that plan rather than replacing it.

faqs.question: Who is Into Action Recovery 113B for?

answer_blocks.text: Adult men with alcohol or drug addiction who need to live away from home to stop, including men who have relapsed after earlier treatment. recovery.com lists alcohol, opioids, fentanyl, cocaine, prescription drugs and repeated relapse for this house.

faqs.question: Can I go out during my stay?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, with the house at first and on your own later. Staff take residents to meetings, shopping, walks and hikes. After the restriction period you can ask for personal outings and weekend passes.
